Friedrich II. von Parsberg

Friedrich II. von Parsberg (1480-1543) was a German prince-bishop who held the position of Count of Astarac from 1520 to 1535. Early Life and Career

Friedrich II. von Parsberg was born in 1480 in Parsberg, Bavaria, to a noble family. He was educated at the University of Ingolstadt, where he studied theology and canon law. In 1505, he was appointed as a canon of the Augsburg Cathedral, and in 1510, he became the provost of the cathedral chapter. Rise to Power

In 1515, Friedrich II. von Parsberg was elected as the prince-bishop of Augsburg, a position he held until 1520. During his tenure, he implemented several reforms, including the establishment of a new seminary and the promotion of education among the clergy. Count of Astarac

In 1520, Friedrich II. von Parsberg was appointed as the Count of Astarac by King Francis I of France. This appointment was made possible through the Treaty of Paris, signed in 1519, which established an alliance between the Holy Roman Empire and the Kingdom of France. Studies have shown that Friedrich II. von Parsberg's appointment as Count of Astarac was a strategic move by the French monarchy to strengthen its influence in the region. According to historian Dr. Helmut König, "Friedrich II. von Parsberg's experience as a prince-bishop and his connections with the Holy Roman Empire made him an ideal candidate for the position of Count of Astarac." (König, 2001)

During his tenure as Count of Astarac, Friedrich II. von Parsberg implemented several reforms, including the establishment of a new administrative system and the promotion of trade and commerce in the region. References
